column2: Levi's ancestral heads approach Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun and Israel's tribal ancestral-house heads; the distinct leadership descriptions remain.
The request at Shiloh in Canaan cites the Lord through Moses and distinguishes residence cities from surrounding lands for livestock; ktene is already broad livestock.
Israel gives cities and surrounding lands to the Levites in the inheritance assignment by the Lord's command; the temporal setting is retained.
Kohath's lot gives Aaron's priestly Levites thirteen cities from Judah, Simeon and Benjamin, preserving the triple designation and three donors.
The remaining Kohathites receive ten cities by lot from Ephraim, Dan and half-Manasseh; the distinction from Aaron's group remains.
Gershon receives thirteen from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Manasseh's Bashan half; no by-lot phrase absent in this selected line is inserted.
Merari's divisions receive twelve by lot from Reuben, Gad and Zebulun, in the selected donor order.
The command-compliance summary repeats cities, surrounding lands and allotment by lot; repetition is retained.
Judah, Simeon and some from Benjamin give the cities; the assignment construction continues into the next unit rather than being supplied with a different city-naming formula.
Aaron's sons are located within Kohath and Levi; because the lot belonged to them remains without adding first, absent here.
Kiriath-arbok is the Anakim's mother-city, Hebron in Judah's mountain. The adversative surrounding-lands phrase continues into the grant to Caleb's sons in 21:12.
Joshua gives the surrounding lands, fields and villages to the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh. The sons and the cross-unit attachment are retained despite the following allocation's tension.
column3: The relation of these surrounding lands to Aaron's allotted lands at 21:13 needs textual/geographical review; no redistribution is imposed.

column2: Aaron's group receives Hebron as refuge for the killer and Libnah, each with allotted lands; this term represents aphorismena, distinct from perisporia surrounding lands.
Ailom and Tema each retain the repeated allotted-lands clause; Ailom is not normalized to Aijalon later in the list.
Gella and Debir each retain their allotted lands in the selected order.
Asa, Tany and Bethsamys complete nine cities from the two tribes, with all three allotted-lands clauses preserved.
Benjamin supplies Gibeon and Gathet with their respective allotted lands; the selected second name is retained.
Anathoth and Gamala complete Benjamin's four cities, each with allotted lands; Gamala is not replaced by a familiar alternate.
Aaron's priestly cities total thirteen, agreeing with nine plus four; the short selected summary adds no lands clause.
The remaining Kohathite divisions receive a city of their territory from Ephraim; the selected singular city remains despite the plural enumeration to follow.
column3: The singular city's relation to the following four-city group is unresolved and is not silently regularized.

column2: Shechem is refuge for the killer and has allotted lands; Gazara retains both what belonged to it and its allotted lands, preserving the doubled expression.
Kabsaïm and Upper Beth-horon complete four Ephraim cities with allotted lands; Upper remains explicit.
Dan provides Elkothaim and Gethedan, each with allotted lands; selected names remain distinct from other city lists.
Aijalon and Gath-rimmon complete four cities from Dan, preserving both land clauses.
Half-Manasseh supplies Taanach and Jebatha, with allotted lands, totaling two.
The remaining Kohathite divisions receive ten cities and lands, agreeing with four plus four plus two.
Gershon receives Gaulon in Bashan and Bosora from half-Manasseh, two cities with allotted lands. The selected plural cities set apart for killers remains, not reduced to one refuge city.
column3: The plural refuge designation applied before the pair differs from the singular forms nearby; preserve it pending apparatus review.

column2: Issachar provides Kison and Debba, each with allotted lands; Debba remains the selected form.
Remmath and Spring of Letters complete four Issachar cities; the translated spring name and both land clauses remain.
Asher provides Basellan and Dabbon, each with allotted lands, without name harmonization.
Helkath and Rehob complete Asher's four cities with allotted lands; Rehob is the inherited conventional representation of the selected Raab form.
Kedesh in Galilee is singularly set apart for the killer; Emmath and Themmon complete three Naphtali cities, all with allotted lands.
Gershon's divisional total thirteen agrees with two plus four plus four plus three; the selected short summary is retained.
Merari's remaining Levites receive Maan and Kedesh from Zebulun; the source returns to perisporia, rendered surrounding lands.
Dimnah and Sella complete four Zebulun cities, each with surrounding lands.
Reuben's trans-Jordan allocation opposite Jericho names refuge Bosor in the wilderness of Misor and Jazer, with surrounding lands; the full selected unit remains.
Dekmon and Mapha complete Reuben's four cities with surrounding lands; neither name is normalized to another list.
Gad supplies refuge Ramoth in Gilead and Kamin, each with surrounding lands.
Heshbon and Jazer complete Gad's four cities; Jazer remains here as well as in the Reuben list, without claiming two distinct identified locations.
Merari's remaining Levite divisions have twelve cities, agreeing with the three four-city groups; territorial wording remains in the conclusion.
The forty-eight Levitical cities within Israel's possession agree with thirteen, ten, thirteen and twelve; surrounding lands continues into the next unit.
Around these cities, each city and its surrounding lands, and all these cities retain the selected repetitive enclosure formula.
Joshua's completion of the land division remains as the first separate lettered unit before the gift narrative.
Israel gives Joshua a portion by the Lord's command; the three giving clauses and requested Thamnasarach in Ephraim's mountain remain, rather than being compressed as duplicate history.
Joshua builds and inhabits the city in a separate short lettered unit.
Joshua takes the stone knives used to circumcise those born on the wilderness journey and places them in Thamnasarach; the full selected continuation remains here.
The Lord gives all the sworn land, and Israel inherits and inhabits it; divine promise and human receipt remain distinct actions.
Rest all around, the oath to the fathers, no enemy rising and the Lord's handing over all enemies remain, preserving the repeated universal language.
No good word fails and all comes to pass; the negative and positive fulfillment clauses remain paired.
Joshua summons Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh in the selected order.
The hear/heed response to Moses and obedience to Joshua's voice retain both authorities and both all-that clauses.
Not forsaking the brothers through the extended days until today and keeping the Lord's command remain two coordinated claims.
Our God and our brothers retain Joshua's inclusive first-person wording; return to homes and the trans-Jordan possession granted by Moses follows the rest announcement.
Replace initial Only with But for alla, preserving the contrasting exhortation without an unsupported exclusive limit. The us commanded by Moses, your God, all His ways, mind and soul remain.
Joshua blesses and dismisses them, and they go home; all three actions remain.
Moses' Bashan half and Joshua's western half remain distinct grants; Joshua's dismissal and blessing begin the temporal clause completed in 22:8.
The wealth, very much livestock, silver, gold, iron and many garments remain with the division of enemy spoil among brothers; no bronze item is added.
Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh leave Shiloh in Canaan for Gilead, retaining possession, inheritance and the Lord's command through Moses.
Galgala of the Jordan in Canaan remains the location; Gad precedes Reuben in the building clause, and the altar's great visible size remains.
The report retains Behold, Gad/Reuben order, Canaan's border and Gilead of the Jordan, without harmonizing Gilead to the preceding Galgala.
column3: The phrase on the side of Israel renders the compressed peran relation; the precise bank/location remains a geographical question.

column2: All Israel gathers at Shiloh with the purpose of going up to war; no actual battle is asserted.
Phinehas' full Eleazar/Aaron genealogy and high-priest title remain in the mission to the three eastern groups.
Ten leaders accompany him, one from each tribal ancestral house; the ancestral-house leadership and commanders-of-thousands titles remain distinct.
Arrival addresses Gad, Reuben and half-Manasseh in Gilead, preserving the selected order before the accusation.
The whole Lord's congregation accuses the tribes of offence, turning away today and becoming apostates through building their own altar; the question and repeated Lord references remain.
The rhetorical small-thing question about Peor, still-unremoved guilt and the congregation's plague remain, without changing the negative cleansing statement to past completion.
The question about today's turning away precedes the conditional departure and tomorrow's wrath upon all Israel; temporal contrast remains explicit.
The selected condition is a small land, not an unclean land. Crossing into the Lord's possession and inheriting among us precede the two prohibitions and the altar distinction.
Behold and the question recall Achar son of Zerah; the single man and was he alone question remain, without recasting the rhetoric as a flat historical assertion.
column3: The scope and expected answer of the final negative question remain an interpretive issue alongside the Joshua 7 account.

column2: Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh answer Israel's commanders of thousands; the human speakers and recipients remain explicit.
The doubled God titles, He knows/Israel shall know and third-person may He not deliver remain. No second-person divine address is introduced.
column3: The punctuation and predication of the repeated God titles remain provisional; the optative is third person, so Thou would change the selected address.

column2: The conditional altar-building for apostasy and its two sacrificial purposes remain. Replace well-being with deliverance for the working rendering of the selected soteriou ritual phrase.
column3: Deliverance is provisional terminology consistent with 9:2b, not a completed specialist identification of the sacrificial category.

column2: Restore initial But for alla and explicitly render hina me as so that your children may not say. Inherited might expresses fear but leaves the negative purpose implicit. The close draft preserves the elliptical purpose opening; literary It is supplies an English clause frame referring to this action, without adding a new purpose. The nested question continues into 22:25.
column3: The purpose construction and long quotation need human read-aloud review. It is is supplied English grammatical support, not an additional source assertion; your children and our children remain distinct.

column2: The quoted Jordan boundary and denial of a portion lead to the feared alienation of our sons by your sons, so that they do not revere the Lord; all personal contrasts remain.
Building this altar is denied two cultic purposes, offerings and sacrifices; the repeated negatives and distinct categories remain.

The altar's testimony between groups and succeeding generations concerns service before the Lord with three offering categories. Replace sacrifices of well-being with sacrifices of deliverance for the selected soterion phrase; tomorrow's denial is explicitly negated.
column3: The ritual label remains provisional pending specialist review; no category is merged with the preceding generic sacrifices.

column2: The hypothetical future speech retains they shall say, the command Behold, likeness of the Lord's altar, fathers, two denied purposes and the threefold testimony relationship.
column3: The subject of they shall say is implicit and contextually may shift to the answering descendants; it is not silently converted to we or you.

column2: The rejection of departure, present days, repeated Lord references and separate offerings, salamin sacrifices and soteriou sacrifice remain. Change only well-being to deliverance in the last category.
column3: Salamin is the selected opaque form, carried forward from the inherited dagger note; its relation to the adjacent ritual terms remains unresolved and must not be silently equated with them.

column2: Phinehas and all the accompanying congregation leaders hear the three tribes' words and are pleased; the collective response is retained.
Phinehas recognizes the Lord with us, denies the offence and credits the eastern tribes with delivering Israel from the Lord's hand; this striking agency remains.
Phinehas and the leaders return from all three groups in Gilead to Israel in Canaan and report the words; the full route and group repetition remain.
Israel's pleasure, repeated speaking to Israel, blessing Israel's God and renunciation of war remain, followed by they dwelt upon it.
column3: The repeated Israel references and final they/it are not simplified into identified subjects; antecedent resolution remains open.

column2: Joshua names the altar of the three eastern groups and declares its testimony between them that the Lord is their God. The selected Joshua subject remains rather than being changed to the tribes.
column3: The precise name-versus-explanation relationship of testimony remains open; no additional proper altar name is invented.
